title: Mru Aerospace
description: Systems that still run a thousand years after we're gone.
ogTitle: Systems that still run a thousand years after we're gone
ogDescription: Mru is software for systems that cannot be easily maintained or repaired: ocean observatories, offshore and remote sites, spacecraft. When processors fail, it keeps delivering checked results with the ones left, instead of stopping.

title: Mru Field: fault tolerance for remote equipment · Mru Aerospace
description: Runs on the processors already in your enclosure. Votes, compares, then self-checks as they fail, instead of stopping. Linux on ARM and x86.
ogTitle: Mru Field: fault tolerance for hard-to-reach systems

title: Mru Flight: onboard fault tolerance · Mru Aerospace
description: A no_std Rust decision core with Kani proofs, to run as F´ components. Continues on two, then one processor after fixed TMR stops.
ogTitle: Mru Flight: fault tolerance for spacecraft out of reach

title: Mru architecture: the shrinking quorum · Mru Aerospace
description: Why triple redundancy stops at the second failure, how a shrinking quorum continues on what is left, and the six-layer architecture from the whitepaper.
ogTitle: Decline is the baseline: the Mru architecture

title: Use cases for Mru Field · Mru Aerospace
description: Fifteen settings where equipment has two or more processors, runs unattended for months, and a repair visit is slow or costly. Ocean settings first.
ogTitle: Where Mru Field applies

title: Deep-sea observatories · Mru Field
description: Seafloor nodes run on batteries or cable with about one ship visit a year. Mru Field keeps them delivering checked data as processors fail between visits.
ogTitle: Batteries, a cable, and one service visit a year

title: Ocean buoys and moorings · Mru Field
description: Moored buoys run for years on solar power and a satellite link. Mru Field keeps the logger delivering checked data after a processor fails at sea.
ogTitle: Years at sea between services

title: Profiling floats and gliders · Mru Field
description: About 900 Argo floats are replaced each year. Mru Field keeps a float's last months of data trustworthy as its processors and memory fail.
ogTitle: Deployed once, rarely recovered

title: Autonomous underwater vehicles · Mru Field
description: AUVs work out of contact with finite power and no way to swap a board. Mru Field decides which processor to trust so the mission continues.
ogTitle: Out of contact, with no way to swap a board

title: Offshore wind · Mru Field
description: Every offshore repair needs a vessel, a crew and a weather window. Mru Field keeps monitoring and control systems working until the next one.
ogTitle: Every repair needs a vessel and a weather window

title: Remote energy and grid equipment · Mru Field
description: Large transformers take up to 4 years to replace, and sites are far from crews. Mru Field keeps the systems that watch them working as parts fail.
ogTitle: Replacement parts take years

title: Remote telecom sites · Mru Field
description: Relay and cell sites are placed for coverage, not access. Mru Field keeps site controllers reporting after a processor fails, without a truck roll.
ogTitle: Sites placed for coverage, not for access

title: Satellite-linked remote devices · Mru Field
description: 32.5M devices on satellite links by 2029. Small power budgets, links in bytes. Mru Field decides on the device and sends checked results only.
ogTitle: Small power budgets, links measured in bytes

title: Polar stations and sensor networks · Mru Field
description: Polar stations run through winters with no access. Mru Field keeps the record going as parts fail, until the next season's visit.
ogTitle: No access for months of the year

title: Nuclear facility monitoring · Mru Field
description: Access is limited by dose and parts age under radiation. Mru Field keeps non-safety monitoring systems reporting as they degrade.
ogTitle: Access limited by dose

title: Nuclear-waste repositories · Mru Field
description: Repository monitoring must run for decades, then far longer. Mru Field is software designed for that gap, tested in simulation and published openly.
ogTitle: Monitoring for decades, then far longer

title: Long-term archives · Mru Field
description: Storage decays faster than records must last. Mru Field decides what to move to durable media, and checks it, as storage fails.
ogTitle: Storage decays faster than the records must last

title: Volcano and seismic stations · Mru Field
description: Remote stations on solar power matter most when access is hardest. Mru Field keeps them recording as processors fail between visits.
ogTitle: Stations matter most when access is hardest

title: Pipelines · Mru Field
description: Hundreds of kilometers of remote valve and monitoring stations. Mru Field keeps their systems trustworthy as they fail, between patrols.
ogTitle: Hundreds of kilometers of remote stations

title: Rail trackside equipment · Mru Field
description: Trackside condition monitoring sits far from depots and is serviced in short windows. Mru Field keeps it reporting as processors fail.
ogTitle: Far from depots, serviced in short windows

title: Log: papers, results, releases · Mru Aerospace
description: Everything Mru publishes: the whitepaper, simulation results and software releases, each with its method, its limits and how to cite it.
ogTitle: Log

title: Same hardware, 1.34× the useful work · Mru Aerospace
description: 10,000 simulated missions on processors that are never repaired. A shrinking quorum delivers 1.34× the useful work of fixed TMR, never less on any mission.
ogTitle: Same hardware, 1.34× the useful work

title: Mru Flight: a first prototype · Mru Aerospace
description: A no_std Rust core with four Kani proofs and a fault-injection demo. With one replica stuck and one dead: 14,490 correct results vs 8,993 for fixed TMR.
ogTitle: Mru Flight: a first prototype

title: About Mru · Mru Aerospace
description: Mru builds fault-tolerant software for systems that cannot be easily maintained or repaired, on Earth and in orbit. Open research, from Horta, Azores.
ogTitle: About Mru
